title: Union Bank of India - 532477 - Transcript Of Post Earnings Call Held On April 23, 2026

summary.headline: Union Bank of India FY26 net profit INR 18,697 crore; Q4 NIM fell to 2.64% QoQ on rate cut, with management targeting 13-14% credit growth.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 net profit of INR 18,697 crore and a dividend of INR 5 per share (50% of face value), with gross advances up 9.74% YoY but total deposits up only 2.72% YoY. Q4 NIM was 2.64%, down from 2.76% in Q3, which management attributed mainly to the December 2025 repo cut passing through to benchmark-linked loans. The bank set aside an additional INR 700 crore general/standard provision, stated as not affecting net profit or capital, and Q4 profit was supported by a INR 1,567 crore write-off recovery (including a INR 658 crore Sterling Biotech settlement) and a lower employee cost due to a discount-rate change. Management said CASA rose to 35.21% from 32.51% in September 2025, and that bulk deposits were reduced by about INR 70,000 crore.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 16.75% YoY; management said more than 99% of retail and other portfolio is at CIBIL score 700 and above.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 18.75% YoY; MSME gross NPA stated at about 4.2%, roughly flat with 10-15 bps movement, with slippages concentrated in a few energy-sensitive cases such as Morbi.

segments.name: Large corporate
segments.commentary: Management shed about INR 35,000 crore of low-yield IBPC (now zero) and about INR 30,000 crore of advances below 6%; a pipeline of INR 50,000-60,000 crore was cited, and over 95% of exposures of INR 25 crore and above are BBB and above.

segments.name: Treasury / investments
segments.commentary: Treasury book reduced by about INR 25,000 crore to fund loan growth; AFS reserve fell about INR 800 crore QoQ to a negative INR 1,008 crore balance, per the call.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth target of 13-14% for FY27, which management said is on track and above industry.
Management said it expects NIM to move positive from 2.64% and to defend or better that level, though it did not give a numeric target.
Management said NII growth should track advances growth in the coming year, assuming a status-quo rate cycle, per the Q&A.
Credit cost guidance kept at around 1% for the year, with FY26 credit cost of about 23 bps cited by analyst.
PSLC fee income: management intends to deploy in FY27 but would not commit to the INR 1,000 crore-plus run-rate of the prior year until SMF and portfolio assessment is complete.

New LCR guidelines: management estimated a negative impact of about INR 14,000 crore and a positive impact of about INR 21,000 crore, a net gain of about INR 7,000 crore (about 3 percentage points of LCR).
capex_capacity: Management did not discuss capex or branch capacity in the call.
Infrastructure bonds of INR 3,000 crore raised in the period; management said a larger bond and capital issuance plan will follow once the board and AGM approve it.
Board-fixed LCR trigger and breach levels are in place; management said LCR is held about 7-8% above these levels.
demand_pricing: Management said deposits were mobilised mainly in January-February 2026 because March bulk and CD rates were elevated, with the blended bulk deposit rate for the quarter at about 6.9-7%.
Management said the incremental blended cost of CASA plus retail term deposit (about INR 1.10 lakh crore added) is about 4.7%; the March 2026 maturing bulk-deposit cost was about 7.70%.
Loan book mix by benchmark: about 54% external-benchmark linked, about 36% MCLR, per the CFO.
Yield on advances cited at 7.98% by analyst; corporate loans priced lower than the average.
Remittance flows have declined and energy-sensitive sectors (for example, commercial gas users in Morbi) were affected; management said trade-relief measures had only 59 applications.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth be 13-14% in FY27, and how will ALM match deposits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed 13-14% credit growth is achievable; it said the bank is funding growth via CASA, retail term deposits, and treasury reallocation, with CD ratio at about 80.4% and LCR at about 114%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall and operating expenses rise in Q4, and how large was the write-off recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed lower establishment cost to a discount-rate change (7.07% to 7.87%) that reduced the year-end liability, and said opex rose from the year-end budget gap of INR 200-300 crore. Write-off recovery was about INR 1,567 crore, including the INR 658 crore Sterling Biotech settlement.

qa_highlights.question: Will stress build from the West Asia war, given slippages of INR 2,023 crore and higher SMA-1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has seen nothing unusual so far, and that SMA-2 accounts moved into SMA-1 after installment recovery, which it views as a better signal. MSME slippages rose only marginally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook and what drove the NIM decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NIM drop from 2.76% to 2.64% QoQ mainly to the December rate cut, and said it expects to hold and ideally improve from that level, supported by CASA growth and lower-yielding book runoff.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL shortfall and what is the INR 700 crore provision for?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ECL shortfall is about INR 4,300 crore, unchanged, and that the INR 700 crore provision is a separate buffer that does not reduce capital or net profit; it is held for the ECL transition or any contingency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the written-off pool and will recoveries be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Written-off pool is about INR 71,000 crore, with roughly INR 45,000-46,000 crore under NCLT; management expects the recovery trend to continue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will NII growth track loan growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NII lagged in Q4 because of the rate cut and endeavours to grow NII in line with advances, assuming a stable rate cycle.

risks_watch: NIM: Q4 at 2.64% after the December rate cut, with the CFO saying 53-58% of loans are linked to external benchmarks; the trajectory in Q1 FY27 is key.

Deposit franchise: the bank relies on retail term deposits and CASA for growth, with a bulk-deposit reliance (about 6.9-7%) that may return if rates are volatile; FY26 deposit growth was 2.72% vs advances 9.74%.

LCR and liquidity headroom: LCR fell to about 114% from about 123% a year earlier, and the new LCR framework's net impact is positive (about +7,000 crore) but management flagged limited room if deposits fall short.
Asset quality: Q4 fresh slippages of INR 2,023 crore vs INR 1,660 crore in Q3, SMA-1 almost doubled per the analyst, and West Asia exposure in energy-sensitive MSME sectors.
Credit cost: management kept a 1% guidance, and FY26 credit cost of about 23 bps is viewed as potentially unsustainable by the analyst.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, CASA, and capital, but defensive and sometimes evasive on margin trajectory, bulk-deposit rates, and the purpose of the INR 700 crore provision. Management repeatedly stressed quality and cost discipline and did not commit to a numeric NIM target.
key_quotes: So, we are choosing growth with quality, number one, and with profitability.
And if you see the NIM of our bank which was 2.91 is right now at 2.70, that is only 21 bps.
It will not decline because this is separate.
Written off pool, if you are looking at it, is around INR 71,000 crores actually.

growth.why: Management targets 13-14% credit growth for FY27 (midpoint 13.5%), backed by a INR 50,000-60,000 crore large-corporate pipeline, RAM advances up 12.56% YoY and 3,000 crore infrastructure bonds, but no new capacity is being added since capex was not discussed and the NIM outlook is only qualitative.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM fell to 2.64% in Q4 from 2.76% in Q3 after the December rate cut; management expects to hold and ideally improve from that level with no numeric target, and CASA rose to 35.21% from 32.51% in Sep 2025, while 53-58% of loans are external-benchmark linked and the blended bulk deposit cost is about 6.9-7%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 13-14% credit growth for FY27 versus 9.74% gross advances growth in FY26, backed by a INR 50,000-60,000 crore large-corporate pipeline and RAM advances up 12.56% YoY (retail 16.75%, MSME 18.75%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management did not discuss capex or branch capacity; only a INR 3,000 crore infrastructure bond was raised and a larger bond and capital plan will follow board and AGM approval.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric NIM target and guided only qualitatively; the 13-14% credit growth target is the only numeric guide and the FY26 deposit growth of 2.72% trails advances growth of 9.74%, limiting room to raise guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 slippages rose to INR 2,023 crore from INR 1,660 crore in Q3, FY26 credit cost of about 23 bps is viewed as potentially unsustainable against the ~1% guide, and the LCR fell to about 114% from about 123% a year earlier.

rows.label: Write-off recoveries sustained into FY27
rows.why: Written-off pool is about INR 71,000 crore (about INR 45,000-46,000 crore under NCLT) and management expects the recovery trend to continue, after Q4 recoveries of INR 1,567 crore including the INR 658 crore Sterling Biotech settlement.

rows.label: Deposit growth must catch up with advances
rows.why: FY26 deposit growth was 2.72% against advances growth of 9.74%, and the CD ratio rose to about 80.4% from about 74%, so funding 13-14% credit growth depends on CASA and retail term deposits.

rows.label: New LCR framework net gain
rows.why: Management estimates a negative impact of about INR 14,000 crore and a positive impact of about INR 21,000 crore, a net gain of about INR 7,000 crore (about 3 percentage points of LCR).

tone.note: Management was confident on credit growth, CASA, capital and recoveries but defensive on the NIM trajectory, bulk-deposit rates and the purpose of the INR 700 crore provision; analysts pushed on margins, the sustainability of the 23 bps credit cost and the rise in SMA-1 and slippages.
